The Three Domain System
¨Up until 20thcentury, only 2 kingdoms –Plantae or Animalia
¤By 1969, 5 kingdoms considered to encompass all life
¤Sequencing of rRNA suggests that all organisms evolved along three distinct lineages,
  nSo different they needed to be categorized in a level broader than kingdom
¨Domain Bacteria
¤Prokaryotic unicellular organisms that reproduce asexually.
¤Cyanobacteria are large photosynthetic prokaryotes.
¤Most bacteria are heterotrophic (break down organic remains)
¤Important in ecosystems -keeping chemical cycling going.
¤Some bacteria are parasitic and cause disease.
explanation: Historically, classification systems evolved from recognizing only two kingdoms (Plantae and Animalia) up to the 20th century, to accepting a five-kingdom system by 1969. Later, sequencing of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) revealed that all life evolved along three distinct lineages that were so different they required a level of classification broader than kingdom: the Domain. Domain Bacteria contains prokaryotic, unicellular organisms that reproduce asexually. It includes cyanobacteria, which are large photosynthetic prokaryotes, and heterotrophic bacteria, which break down organic remains and are vital for sustaining chemical cycling in ecosystems. Some bacterial species are parasitic and cause disease.

questions.q: What molecular evidence led scientists to establish the three-domain system over the five-kingdom system?
opts: Analysis of Hox gene activation timing
questions.exp: Sequencing of rRNA suggested that all organisms evolved along three distinct lineages that were genetically different enough to warrant a level broader than kingdom (domains).

questions.q: Which of the following is a key characteristic of organisms in Domain Bacteria?
opts: They are prokaryotic unicellular organisms that reproduce asexually.
They all possess a membrane-bounded nucleus.
They reproduce exclusively through sexual reproduction.
questions.exp: Domain Bacteria consists of prokaryotic, unicellular organisms that reproduce asexually.
